samples.summary: Held render now consumes `dirtyBlockIds`, so the replayed render after every undo unit is a FULL document relayout (per keystroke)
samples.evidence: `this.requestLayoutRefresh?.()` (text-editor.ts:738) is wired to `recomputeLayout` (editor.ts:2531). `recomputeLayout` ends with `dirtyBlockIds = undefined` (editor.ts:1534). In `handleInput` the last statement inside the unit is `this.requestRender()` (text-editor.ts:1046), which is held and therefore runs `recomputeLayout()` — consuming and clearing the dirty set. `withUndoUnit`'s finally then replays `this.requestRender()` → host `render()` → `recomputeLayout()` again, this time with `dirtyBlockIds === undefined`. In `computeLayout`, `canUseCache = cache != null && dirtyBlockIds != null && ...` (layout.ts:456-459), so a null dirty set disables the incremental cache entirely and every block in the document is re-measured. Result: each keystroke/Enter/paste/backspace-over-selection now costs one incremental pass plus one O(document) full layout pass, instead of a single incremental pass. This defeats the incremental relayout the docs rendering-optimization design (and `test/view/cursor-move-no-relayout.test.ts`) exists to protect. Fix: have the mid-unit refresh preserve/accumulate `dirtyBlockIds`, or make the post-unit replay paint-only since the layout is already fresh.

samples.summary: With the blessed `snapshot()`-then-`batch()` ordering, a batch that writes nothing still loses the redo stack on MemDocStore
samples.evidence: `batch()` restores `this.redoStack = priorRedo` when nothing was written (memory.ts:253), but `priorRedo` is captured *after* the preceding `snapshot()` already did `this.redoStack = []` (memory.ts:183). The delta's own comments assert that the outside-the-batch snapshot ordering `TextEditor.withUndoUnit()` uses "costs nothing on `MemDocStore` either" and that only an inside call means "nothing can disturb the redo stack" (memory.ts:206-219, link-run.ts:80-88, text-editor.ts:3830-3836). It does cost something: on a MemDocStore host (slides text box, docs demo) an action that goes `saveSnapshot()` → `withUndoUnit(body that writes nothing)` — e.g. Enter/type paths whose body turns out to be a no-op — clears redo, while `YorkieDocStore.snapshot()` is a no-op and keeps `doc.history`'s redo stack. The two stores are documented as sharing one contract; here they diverge, and the user silently loses redo.

samples.summary: A layout exception now throws from inside the store batch, rolling back the whole user edit on YorkieDocStore
samples.evidence: `requestLayoutRefresh?.()` is invoked from the `requestRender` wrapper while `undoUnitDepth > 0`, i.e. inside `this.doc.batch(fn)` (text-editor.ts:735-741, 3822). `recomputeLayout` runs the full `computeLayout`/`paginateLayout` pass over a transiently mid-action document (empty block list, half-rewritten table cells). Any throw there now propagates out of the batch body; `YorkieDocStore.batch()` runs the body inside one `doc.update`, so Yorkie discards the clone (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2929-2948) and the user's entire edit is dropped rather than partially committed. Before this delta the held render ran after commit, so a layout failure could not undo the write.

samples.summary: Adoption check adds an extra whole-document JSON.stringify to every batch
samples.evidence: `const adopted = top !== undefined && JSON.stringify(top) === beforeJson;` (memory.ts:223) serializes the previous undo checkpoint in full on every top-level `batch()`, on top of the two serializations the `wroteNothing` comparison already does. It is also fragile: the comparison is key-order sensitive, so a document whose live object happens to have differently-ordered keys than its clone silently falls back to the old double-checkpoint (dead Cmd+Z) behaviour with no signal.

verdict.reason: The described chain exists exactly as claimed and is reachable on ordinary typing. text-editor.ts:733-742 makes a held render still call requestLayoutRefresh; editor.ts:2531 binds that to recomputeLayout, which consumes dirtyBlockIds (editor.ts:1526) and then unconditionally clears it (editor.ts:1534). withUndoUnit's finally replays requestRender at depth 0 (text-editor.ts:3845-3847), which reaches hostRequestRender = renderWithScroll (editor.ts:2473, 2434-2438) -> render() = recomputeLayout(); paint() (editor.ts:2208-2211), synchronously, with no rAF coalescing. On that second pass dirtyBlockIds is undefined, so canUseCache is false (layout.ts:456-459), the cache-hit branch at layout.ts:535 is skipped, and every block is re-measured via layoutBlock (layout.ts:538) — an O(document) pass per keystroke, on top of the incremental pass. handleInput is a live path with this shape (markDirty at text-editor.ts:1034, held requestRender as the last in-unit statement at text-editor.ts:1046), as are Enter/split (2651) and paste (4247, 5882). Nothing re-marks or preserves the dirty set between the two passes; invalidateLayout (editor.ts:1673-1676) only clears more state. The existing perf guard test only covers caret moves (cursor-move-no-relayout.test.ts:121-138), so it does not make this unreachable. This breaks the documented incremental-relayout invariant (docs/design/docs/docs-rendering-optimization.md:174-246) on a normal-use path, which is in the correctness lane; I found no ground to refute.

finding.summary: `saveSnapshot()` outside the new batch doubles every undo entry on `MemDocStore` — a dead Cmd+Z per edit
finding.evidence: Every new unit follows the shape `this.saveSnapshot(); this.withUndoUnit(() => {...})` (lines 814/816, 995/1001, 1532/1533, 2655/2656, 2695/2696, 4220/4221, plus `deleteSelection()`'s implicit unit at 3836 reached from 2483/2534/2583/2604/883/3408). `saveSnapshot` is wired to `docStore.snapshot()` (editor.ts:2475, text-box-editor.ts:680). `MemDocStore.snapshot()` only short-circuits when `batchDepth > 0` (store/memory.ts:181), and `MemDocStore.batch()` then pushes its OWN checkpoint unconditionally (store/memory.ts:206-209). So on the memory store one keystroke now leaves `undoStack = [..., A, A]`: the first Cmd+Z restores the pre-edit state, the second consumes an entry and changes nothing (and redo needs two presses too). The repo already spells this out: link-run.ts:81-85 — "`snapshot` … runs *inside* the batch … a call before the batch costs a second, identical undo step (a dead Cmd+Z)" — and `withNamedStyleChange` (editor.ts:1238-1239) puts `snapshot()` inside for exactly that reason. MemDocStore is the store for the slides text-box editor (text-box-editor.ts:431) and standalone docs mounts, so this is a live path. The Yorkie constraint (presence must be flushed outside the batch) is real, but it makes the two stores need different placement, which this change does not reconcile.

verdict.reason: The finding rests on the claim that MemDocStore.batch() pushes its own checkpoint unconditionally, so a saveSnapshot() immediately before withUndoUnit leaves two identical undo entries. The code does not do that. memory.ts:220-227 computes `adopted = top !== undefined && JSON.stringify(top) === beforeJson` and only pushes when `!adopted`, i.e. a snapshot taken immediately before the batch (same document state, nothing written in between) is adopted as the batch's own "before" and no second entry is created. The explanatory comment at memory.ts:207-219 names this exact ordering, and test/store/memory.test.ts:317-337 pins it: snapshot() then a two-write batch(), one undo() restores 'Hello' and canUndo() is false — one unit, no dead Cmd+Z. The reviewer's supporting quote is also inverted: link-run.ts:81-89 states that MemDocStore.batch() "adopts an identical checkpoint taken immediately before it rather than doubling it", the opposite of the quoted claim. The call sites match the adoption precondition (e.g. text-editor.ts:1013 saveSnapshot() directly followed by withUndoUnit() at 1019, and withUndoUnit at 3839-3850 does nothing but doc.batch(fn)). The alleged Yorkie/memory placement conflict is reconciled inside MemDocStore.batch().

finding.summary: Holding interior `requestRender()` leaves the layout (and `blockParentMap`) stale for the rest of the undo unit; the paste path branches on it
finding.evidence: `render()` is synchronous — `recomputeLayout(); paint();` (editor.ts:2208-2211) — and `getLayout()` returns the `layout` variable that only `recomputeLayout()` reassigns (`invalidateLayout()` at editor.ts:1673 merely drops the cache, it does not refresh `layout`). Before this change, `deleteSelectionImpl`'s trailing `this.requestRender()` (lines 3910/3944/3995/4031/4060) refreshed the layout before the caller's remaining work ran. The new wrapper (718-724) swallows it until the outermost unit closes, so everything after `deleteSelection()` inside a unit now reads a PRE-delete layout. Concretely in `applyPastePlan` (1533-1539): `pasteTableCells` reads `this.getLayout().blockParentMap.get(pos.blockId)` (4416-4418) and `insertBlocks` reads `this.isInCell(pos.blockId)` (4291 → 3663, same map). The cell-range delete branch replaces each selected cell's blocks with FRESH ids (3927-3932) and parks the cursor on one of them (3938-3941); that id is absent from the stale map, so `cellInfo` is undefined, the code takes the "cursor not in a table" branch, `this.doc.getBlockIndex(pos.blockId)` returns -1 for a cell-internal block (model/document.ts:271-273) and `insertBlockAt(0, tableBlock)` (4436) drops the pasted table at the top of the body instead of into the cell that was just cleared. The mirror risk is a stale map that still resolves a *deleted* `tableBlockId`, where `this.doc.getBlock(tableBlockId)` (4445) throws (Doc.getBlock throws on a miss) inside the batch — under Yorkie that rolls the whole paste back.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. The held-render wrapper does not merely swallow the render: text-editor.ts:733-742 sets `renderAfterUndoUnit` and then unconditionally calls `this.requestLayoutRefresh?.()` before returning, with the inline comment "Paint later, measure now — the remainder of the unit reads getLayout()". The docs host wires that seam at editor.ts:2531 (`textEditor.requestLayoutRefresh = recomputeLayout;`), and `recomputeLayout` (editor.ts:1510-1580) is the very same function the pre-change synchronous `render()` ran (editor.ts:2208-2211): it reassigns `layout` (1532), re-paginates (1535) and rebuilds/installs the merged `blockParentMap` via `doc.setBlockParentMap` (1572-1579). So after `deleteSelectionImpl`'s interior `this.requestRender()` (e.g. text-editor.ts:3936) inside the paste unit, `getLayout().blockParentMap` is refreshed exactly as before the change — only the paint is deferred. The claimed downstream consequences in `applyPastePlan` (text-editor.ts:1543-1568) → `pasteTableCells` / `insertBlocks` (stale map → cellInfo undefined → insertBlockAt(0), or a stale map resolving a deleted tableBlockId into a throwing `doc.getBlock`) therefore rest on a premise the source contradicts. The one host that leaves `requestLayoutRefresh` unwired is the slides text-box editor (text-box-editor.ts:668-705), whose host render is rAF-scheduled and which has no tables, so the table-paste branch is not reachable there. The reviewer's own quoted line range (718-724) is the constructor's field-assignment block, not the wrapper.
